questions.text:
A festival of light and sound has been organised in the local high school. The school entrance has a temporary water feature and guide ropes to direct visitors into the building.

The water feature looks like a long water tank with one shallow end and one deep end. Joe notices a series of waves moving along the water surface. They move from left to right.

Name the physics phenomenon that causes the changes in the waves shown in the diagram, as they move from left to right.

The waves are generated at the left-hand end, at a rate of 6 waves in 8.0 seconds. The initial wavelength of the waves is 4.0 cm, and this reduces to 2.0 cm at the right-hand end.

Calculate the final velocity of the waves just as they hit the wall on the right-hand end.
questions.markingGuide: f = 6/8 = 0.75 Hz. λ₁ = 0.04 m. Speed in deep = v₁ = fλ₁ = 0.75 × 0.04 = 0.03 m s⁻¹. Using v₂/v₁ = λ₂/λ₁: v₂/0.03 = 0.02/0.04. Speed in shallow = v₂ = 0.015 m s⁻¹. Achieved: Correct frequency. Merit: Correct answer.

questions.text:
Describe and explain the phenomenon identified in part (a), as the wave moves from left to right.

Include a description of any changes to wavelength, velocity, amplitude, and frequency of the waves.
questions.expectedAnswer: The wave slows down as it enters shallow water.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Any TWO correct points. Merit: THREE correct points clearly linked. Excellence: Explanation including all FOUR bullet points.

questions.text:
The guide ropes beyond the water feature consist of a less dense rope joined to a more dense rope. A student sends a pulse down the rope from the left along the less dense rope to the right.

Complete the diagram to show both the transmitted and reflected pulse after the pulse hits the boundary between the ropes.

You should include labels that identify the transmitted pulse and the reflected pulse.
questions.expectedAnswer: Reflected pulse: opposite phase, smaller amplitude, further from boundary than transmitted pulse.
questions.markingGuide: Evidence: Reflected pulse has opposite phase. Transmitted pulse same phase. Both amplitudes smaller than incident. Reflected pulse further from boundary. Achieved: Any of the bullet points on diagram. OR stated reflected pulse is faster. Merit: THREE bullet points on diagram AND stated reflected pulse is faster. Excellence: Correct, fully labelled diagram with arrows AND correct comparison of velocities.

questions.text: Compare the velocity of the reflected pulse with that of the transmitted pulse.
questions.expectedAnswer: The reflected pulse is faster than the transmitted pulse.

questions.text:
A room has been set up with mirrors and lenses to create different images. Anaru looks closely into a large curved mirror. His image is enlarged and upright.

State the third property of the image.

Anaru is 1.5 m tall and is standing 0.90 m in front of the mirror, which has a focal length of 2.0 m.

Calculate the height of the image.
questions.expectedAnswer: hᵢ = 2.7 m (accept without the negative sign)
questions.markingGuide: 1/f = 1/dᵢ + 1/dₒ. 1/2 = 1/dᵢ + 1/0.9. dᵢ = −1.636 m. dᵢ/dₒ = hᵢ/hₒ → −1.636/0.9 = hᵢ/1.5 → hᵢ = −2.7 m. Accept without the negative. Achieved: Correct dᵢ. Merit: Correct answer.

questions.text:
Joe stands 4.0 m in front of the concave mirror with focal length 2.0 m.

Complete the ray diagram below to locate the image.
questions.expectedAnswer: Image is inverted, real, same size as object, located at dᵢ = 4.0 m (= 2f).
questions.markingGuide: dₒ = 4, dᵢ = 4. hₒ = 2, hᵢ = −2. Achieved: Correct nature of image: real, same size, and inverted. OR ONE correct ray drawn. Merit: Correct ray diagram (with arrows). Excellence: Correct ray diagram (with arrows) correctly locating image AND image described.

questions.text: State the three properties of the image formed.
questions.expectedAnswer: Inverted, real image, same size as object (hᵢ = hₒ), dᵢ = 2f.

questions.text:
A candle is set up in front of a convex lens. The image produced is projected onto the screen, and is inverted and diminished.

State the property of the image that allows it to be projected on to a screen.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Real image is produced. OR one correct ray drawn from an object. OR move the candle closer to the lens to enlarge the object (not within f).

questions.text: Complete a ray diagram on the axis below to show how the inverted and diminished image could be formed.
questions.expectedAnswer: Object placed beyond 2F, two correct rays drawn, image between F and 2F on other side, inverted...
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Real image is produced. OR one correct ray drawn. OR move candle closer to lens (not within f). Merit: TWO of: image is real, two rays with arrows, bring object closer. Excellence: All THREE: image is real, two rays with arrows and labels, bring object closer to lens (not within f).

questions.text:
The boys move the candle to produce a larger image, still able to be formed on a screen.

Explain how the image size can be made larger and still formed on a screen.
questions.expectedAnswer: Bring object closer to the lens (but not within f).
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Bring object closer to the lens.

questions.text:
The final room is filled with a light display using fibre optics.

A fibre optic cable is made from a glass core contained within a cladding (covering).

State what the symbols n₁ and n₂ represent in the diagram above.
Name the phenomenon that allows light rays to be transmitted along the fibre optic cable.
State the conditions required for this phenomenon to occur within this fibre optic cable.
questions.expectedAnswer: The angle of incidence on the glass-cladding boundary must be greater than the critical angle
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: (i) OR either of the points from part (ii). Merit: Correct answer — (ii) must be in the context of glass and cladding.

questions.text:
A table has been set up with a single beam of light shining through a tank that is filled with oil. The light is moving from the oil into the air.

Add a labelled arrow to the diagram to show the refracted ray as light passes from oil to air.
questions.expectedAnswer: Ray bending away from normal in air, with label and arrow.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Ray bending away from normal in air. OR n₁ = 1.17. OR finds angle from incorrect n. Merit: TWO of: correct ray, correct angle, correct n. Excellence: Correct answer including refracted ray with label and arrow.

questions.text:
The angle of incidence on the oil-air boundary is 30°.
The refractive index of air is 1.00.
The velocity of light in air: v₁ = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹
and in oil: v₂ = 2.56 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹

Calculate the angle of refraction in air.
questions.markingGuide: n₁ = v₁/v₂ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 2.56 × 10⁸ = 1.17. n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂. 1.17 × sin 30 = 1 × sin θ₂. θ₂ = 35.8°. Achieved: Ray bending away from normal in air. OR n = 1.17. Merit: TWO of: correct ray, correct angle, correct n. Excellence: Correct answer including refracted ray with label and arrow.

questions.text:
As the people leave, they pass a signal generator set up with two loudspeakers lined up. The speakers are both sounding the same single frequency at the same volume.

The people walk past the speakers.

Describe and explain any changes to the sound experienced by the people as they walk past the speakers.

You may use a diagram to help explain your answer.
questions.expectedAnswer: Visitors hear alternating loud and soft sounds due to constructive and destructive interference,...
questions.markingGuide: Loud sounds due to constructive interference (crest + crest, path difference = whole wavelengths). Quiet zones due to destructive interference (crest + trough, path difference = odd half wavelengths). Achieved: ONE of: loud/constructive, soft/destructive, description of interference, interference linked to path difference, diagram with nodal/anti-nodal line. Merit: An explanation including at least THREE. Excellence: Comprehensive explanation of interference linked to path difference.
